pointers.sentence: `django/utils/deprecation.py` holds the warning classes with which Django marks what it will remove, `RemovedInDjango2028Warning` and `RemovedInDjango2029Warning`, and the helpers that raise them: `warn_about_external_use`, which warns only when the code using a deprecated feature is outside Django, `warn_about_implementation`, which names a definition, and `deprecate_posargs`, which makes parameters keyword-only while still taking them by position for a time.

Django's deprecation policy is written in feature releases: a feature deprecated in A.x keeps working in every A.x release but raises warnings, and is removed in B.0, or in B.1 when it was deprecated in the last A.x, so that a deprecation spans at least two feature releases (`docs/internals/release-process.txt`).
Following DEP 20, the releases planned as 7.0 and 7.1 are Django 2028 and 2029, and each warning class is named for the release that removes what it marks (`docs/releases/6.2.txt`).

The timeline lists under 2028 what 6.0 and 6.1 deprecated, with the new shape of `django.VERSION` that 6.2 announces, and under 2029 the rest of what 6.2 deprecated (`docs/internals/deprecation.txt`).

`RemovedInDjango2028Warning` derives from `DeprecationWarning`, and `RemovedInDjango2029Warning`, the farther off, from `PendingDeprecationWarning` (`django/utils/deprecation.py:RemovedInDjango2028Warning`).

`RemovedInNextVersionWarning` and `RemovedAfterNextVersionWarning` are the same two classes, named by distance rather than year; nothing in the `django` package uses them, and Django's test suite turns both into errors (`tests/runtests.py`).
Code that must change when a deprecation ends but raises no warning carries a comment above it naming the class (`docs/internals/contributing/writing-code/submitting-patches.txt`).
A name the module does not define is looked up in its `__getattr__` (`django/utils/deprecation.py:__getattr__`).

`MiddlewareMixin`, moved to `django/middleware/__init__.py` in 6.2, is answered with a `RemovedInDjango2029Warning` naming the importing line, and imported inside the function, its comment says, so that importing the module does not need `django.middleware`'s dependencies ([Sync and async in one chain](../handlers/async.md)).
`django_file_prefixes` gives the `django` package's directory with a separator at the end, computed once (`django/utils/warnings.py:django_file_prefixes`).

A warning raised with `skip_file_prefixes=django_file_prefixes()` names the first frame above its raiser whose file is not Django's, as `JsonResponse` does when given its deprecated safe argument (`django/http/response.py:JsonResponse.__init__`).
It finds the **effective caller**, the code that used the feature, and warns only if that is outside Django (`django/utils/deprecation.py:warn_about_external_use`).

The deprecated settings pass as prefixes the settings classes and the test utilities that override settings (`django/conf/__init__.py:_show_settings_deprecation_warning`), and `get_connection`, under `deprecate_posargs`, passes `skip_frames=1`, for its wrapper (`django/core/mail/__init__.py:get_connection`).

The deprecated settings pass as prefixes the settings classes and the test utilities that override settings (`django/conf/__init__.py:_show_settings_deprecation_warning`), and `get_connection`, under `deprecate_posargs`, passes `skip_frames=1`, for its wrapper (`django/core/mail/__init__.py:get_connection`).

It takes a function, a class, a bound method, or a classmethod, staticmethod or property object, finds the unwrapped function's file and line with `inspect.getsourcefile` and `inspect.getsourcelines`, and calls `warnings.warn_explicit` with them (`django/utils/deprecation.py:warn_about_implementation`).

`ModelAdmin` uses it for an override of `ModelAdmin.get_actions` without the action_location parameter (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin._get_actions_with_action_location`; [The admin](../admin.md)).

Making a parameter keyword-only breaks every call that passes it by position; `deprecate_posargs` lets the function be written in its final form, after a `*`, and still take the old calls for the period (`django/utils/deprecation.py:deprecate_posargs`).

`RenameMethodsBase` is a metaclass for renaming a method, its docstring citing ticket 15363; a subclass lists triples of old name, new name and warning class in `RenameMethodsBase.renamed_methods` (`django/utils/deprecation.py:RenameMethodsBase`).
